headline: Testing learned neural representations for transfer, editing, and brain alignment
label: Neural Representation Transfer Testing
summary: Recent preprints test whether learned neural representations support counterfactual editing, cross-task transfer, and cross-subject alignment.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit testing of learned representations against editing, transfer, or interpretability criteria. Neural-DISCO applies disentangled representation learning to source-conditioned counterfactual editing of neural population activity. A multitask study trains hierarchical almost-linear RNNs on 100 cognitive tasks to map how tasks transfer or interfere in shared recurrent dynamics, while neuronal identity routing builds latent groups from molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological profiles. On the neuroimaging side, MtReNIRS yields transferable neurovascular representations from 12 public fNIRS datasets, and JEPA-based fMRI encoders enable unsupervised cross-participant alignment. The items share no common method or dataset; what is new is the emphasis on transfer and editing tests.
